result.reviewScopeSummary: Initial verification of Story 0 against AC-5.1 through AC-5.5, the derivation vocabulary rename DoD, v7 migration, public SDK logging surface, logging tests, and production fallback/logging paths.

newFindings.title: Ready derivation rows still persist fallback markers instead of logging fallback events only
newFindings.evidence: AC-5.3 requires a fallback event to exist only in the log and says ready derivation output must carry no degraded/fallback marker (00-foundation.md:43-48). Production turn derivation still collects fallback gaps and attaches them to ready turn_rendering writes (packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:83,95,106-115). Chunk summaries do the same (packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/derive.ts:164-175,192-200). The queue completion path persists those gaps on ready derivation rows (packages/lhc/src/tech-utils/work-queue/index.ts:304-312). `rg writeLog` found no production fallback call sites outside the SDK wrapper and logging tests, and TC-5.3a only manually inserts a clean derivation row before writing a log (packages/lhc/test/logging-surface.test.ts:93-143).
requirementIds: Story 0 DoD: no fallback marker on ready derivation outputs

newFindings.title: writeLog participates in the caller transaction
newFindings.evidence: The story technical notes require `writeLog` to be fail-soft and not share the caller transaction (00-foundation.md:133-134), and DD-5 says it must not share the caller's transaction (tech-design.md:127-129). The implementation inserts through `ctx.db` directly (packages/lhc/src/tech-utils/logging/index.ts:43-59). A focused rollback probe wrote a log inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, rolled back the caller transaction, and observed `{"n":0}` log rows; an independent log transaction would have left one row. TC-5.5a only injects a fake throwing prepare function, so it does not prove real-store transaction isolation (packages/lhc/test/logging-surface.test.ts:220-235).

newFindings.title: Derivation vocabulary rename is not complete across current production/public shapes
newFindings.evidence: Story 0 scope and DoD require the form vocabulary to be renamed across code and schema (00-foundation.md:15-18,162), and DD-1 says every reference changes from form to derivation vocabulary (tech-design.md:87-89). Current shared/public view and inspect shapes still expose `formUsed` and `formCounts` (packages/lhc/src/shared/view.ts:116-125,152; packages/lhc/src/shared/inspect.ts:57,74). The compact production path persists those names into thread_view JSON (packages/lhc/src/domains/thread-view/index.ts:458-479,508-514), and thread-view internals still define `FormSnapshot`/`FormLookup` for derivation state rows (packages/lhc/src/domains/thread-view/internal/render.ts:131-145).
requirementIds: Story 0 Scope In: derivation vocabulary rename
Story 0 DoD: rename complete across schema, types, work-queue kinds, and tests

verified: AC-5.1 / TC-5.1a: info, warning, and error log levels are persisted by the SDK logging path and covered by logging-surface.test.ts.
AC-5.2 / TC-5.2a: internal writeLog and SDK instance logging.write write to the same durable log table in logging-surface.test.ts.
AC-5.3 / TC-5.3b: failed derivation state and reason remain on the derivation row independent of log entries in logging-surface.test.ts.
AC-5.4 / TC-5.4a: queryLog supports level, derivationType, subjectId, and reason filters; logging-surface.test.ts covers mixed-field filtering.
V7 schema migration is registered and story/epic gates pass under user_version 7.
unverified: AC-5.3 / TC-5.3a production path: actual fallback during derivation construction still writes gaps to ready derivation rows and has no production log call site.
AC-5.5 / TC-5.5a transaction containment: writeLog catches write failures, but a real log write shares and rolls back with the caller transaction.
Story 0 derivation vocabulary rename DoD: public/shared thread-view shapes and persisted JSON still use formUsed/formCounts/FormSnapshot vocabulary.

gatesRun.command: cd packages/lhc && pnpm exec vitest run test/logging-surface.test.ts
cd packages/lhc && pnpm exec tsx -e '<writeLog inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, then ROLLBACK; assert log count === 1>'

productionPathFindings: Ready derivation completion still persists fallback `gaps` on derivation rows, so fallback markers remain in the derivation state/output channel instead of only the log.
writeLog uses the caller's DatabaseSync handle and participates in the caller transaction; rollback proof observed zero persisted log rows after caller rollback.
Thread-view compact still persists form vocabulary in arrangement/source-state JSON (`formUsed`, `formCounts`) and exposes it through shared view/inspect surfaces.
additionalObservations: The configured story and epic gates passed, but they do not cover the rollback isolation proof or production fallback-channel behavior.
`verify` and `verify-all` reported 9 skipped real-inference tests because LHC_OPENROUTER_KEY was unset; I did not use those skipped tests as Story 0 evidence.
